findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders empty placeholder instead of real data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is on, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — hardcoded empty columns and empty data — instead of passing the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, and `fields` that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` uses. Any organization with this flag enabled will see completely blank dashboard table widgets (no rows, no headers), losing all data currently displayed. The real table data must be mapped into the new component's `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` shape before this branch can ship.

findings.title: fetch_error_details mispairs error IDs with node data and mixes string/float timestamps
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` where `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node_id. If any requested node is missing, `events.values()` is shorter and shifted, so each `event_id` gets paired with the wrong event's data (wrong title/message/timestamp attributed to the wrong error), and the `id` field on the resulting ErrorEvent is wrong. Additionally, nodestore event data stores `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string, but the code defaults it to `0.0` and later compares/sorts it against breadcrumb float timestamps (`error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` in `gen_request_data`), which raises `TypeError` when comparing str to float in Python 3. The endpoint should iterate `zip(error_ids, (events.get(n) for n in node_ids))` and parse the timestamp to a float (e.g. `datetime.fromisoformat`).

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applied when a search query is present
findings.body: The new `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` exclusion (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is only applied inside the `if (searchQuery.trim())` branch of `sortedAndFilteredAttributes`. When the search box is empty, the full sorted list is returned unchanged, so these internal attributes are still displayed. Worse, the behavior is inconsistent: a user who types a query matching e.g. `project_id` will see the attribute disappear from the results. The filter should be applied before the search filter (i.e., always), not only when searching.

findings.title: Enabled guard `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true and data can be undefined
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams(selection.datetime)` always returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true — the guard does nothing. More importantly, on the success path the hook does `data.numFeedbacksUsed` without checking `data` is defined; if the query resolves without data (e.g. disabled then re-enabled states, or a 204/empty body), `data` can be `undefined` and the hook will throw a TypeError, crashing the feedback list page since the component only guards `isPending`/`isError`. Add a defined check on `data` before accessing its fields.
